title: Build K3s orchestration substrate with RuntimeClasses for firecracker/kata/runc
description: Deploy a K3s lightweight Kubernetes cluster across 3 bare-metal test nodes (96 cores, 512GB RAM, 2TB NVMe each) and register three RuntimeClasses: 'firecracker' (firecracker-containerd handler, node selector features.vmm=firecracker) for T1-T3, 'kata-qemu' for T4-T6 full-system emulation, and 'runc' for T7-T8 containers. Includes namespace helix-testing, ResourceQuota (96 req CPU, 256Gi mem, firecracker.microvm.io/vms=500), ServiceAccount and RBAC Role granting pods/services/chaos-mesh CRD access. GAP_AUDIT marks this MISSING/DEFERRED (no k3s/RuntimeClass in code).
closure_criteria: On a real KVM-enabled host, `kubectl get runtimeclass` lists firecracker/kata-qemu/runc; scheduling a pod under each handler succeeds (Running) where pre-change none existed; capture kubectl output + pod events with a per-run UUID tag proving each RuntimeClass schedules workloads.

title: Implement Firecracker microVM provisioner for T1-T3 with vsock and virtio-net
description: Install Firecracker VMM (v1.5+), build custom kernel vmlinux-5.15-helix with vsock+virtio-net drivers, and create ext4 rootfs for T1 (Desktop 4vCPU/4GB), T2 (Laptop 2vCPU/2GB), T3 (Workstation 8vCPU/8GB). Provisioner configures boot-source, read-only rootfs drive + writable overlay drive, machine-config, tap network interface, and vsock device per the Firecracker JSON config. GAP_AUDIT: MISSING/DEFERRED (no firecracker in .go).
closure_criteria: On a KVM host, the provisioner cold-boots a T1 microVM to a shell where the HelixCluster agent process executes and connects over vsock; before=no VM, after=running agent reachable via vsock; capture boot log + agent ready signal with run UUID.

title: Implement Firecracker golden snapshot create/restore pipeline (<=28ms restore)
description: Build the cold-boot-once-then-snapshot pattern: boot each tier to agent-ready state, pause via Firecracker PATCH /vm, capture Full snapshot (VM state file + memory file) via PUT /snapshot/create, then restore subsequent instances via PUT /snapshot/load + PATCH state=Resumed. Snapshot pool keyed by device template; COW mmap sharing across instances from one base snapshot. Target ~28ms restore, ~50MB compressed snapshot.
closure_criteria: Run 1,000 restore loops from a golden snapshot on a real host and measure p99 restore latency <=28ms; before=cold boot ~1.2s, after=28ms per restore; capture latency histogram (p50/p99) and snapshot file sizes tagged with run UUID.

title: Implement QEMU/KVM ARM64 virt provisioner for T6 RK3588-approximate SBC
description: Provision T6 (Orange Pi 5 Max) via QEMU virt machine: -machine virt,virtualization=on,gic-version=3, -cpu max,pauth-impdef=on,sve=on, -smp 8,clusters=2,cores=4 to approximate Cortex-A76+A55 big.LITTLE, 16GB RAM, AAVMF UEFI bios, virtio-net tap, qcow2 rootfs. Mali-G610 GPU, 6 TOPS NPU, 8K VPU NOT emulated (document the gap). A real QEMU provisioner exists from Phase-1 (containers/pkg/vm/qemu.go) but is not tied to Phase-4 tiers/registry per GAP_AUDIT.
closure_criteria: On an ARM64-capable KVM host, provision a T6 VM that boots to Linux and the agent registers with the controller; before=no node, after=T6 ARM64 node visible in DevicePool; capture agent registration + uname -m=aarch64 with run UUID.

title: Integrate Cuttlefish/CrosVM provisioner for T5 Android AOSP devices
description: Integrate Cuttlefish (CrosVM backend) for T5 Android simulation via launch_cvd (4 vCPU, 4096MB, 8192MB data image, enable_minimal_mode, per-instance num). Supports headless CI use, AOSP framework behavior (Doze/App Standby). Cap concurrent instances at 12/host with health-check retry + Docker-Android fallback (per Risk 2 mitigation).
closure_criteria: Launch a Cuttlefish T5 instance that boots AOSP and exposes ADB; before=no device, after=adb shell reachable and agent running; capture launch_cvd boot completion + adb getprop with run UUID.

title: Implement T4 gaming-console protocol-level constrained x86_64 VM
description: Since QEMU cannot emulate the PlayStation 4 custom AMD APU, provision T4 at the protocol level: the HelixCluster agent runs in a resource-limited x86_64 QEMU VM matching console-class specs (8GB, ~12/host). Hybrid controller must also represent physical PS4 devkits as 'special tier' nodes with uniform health monitoring + chaos injection but excluded from large-scale simulation.
closure_criteria: Provision a T4 protocol VM whose agent responds to a health check and is schedulable; before=no T4 node, after=T4 node passes health check; capture health-check response + tier classification with run UUID.

title: Implement Docker + binfmt_misc protocol stubs for T7 iOS and T8 HarmonyOS
description: Register QEMU binfmt_misc (tonistiigi/binfmt --install all) for cross-arch execution, then run T7 iOS protocol-level ARM64 containers (128MB, 0.5 CPU) and T8 HarmonyOS/OpenHarmony ARM64 containers (256MB, 1.0 CPU). Protocol-only: no true iOS emulation; GPU/NPU/camera/GPS/push require physical hardware. GAP_AUDIT: MISSING (ios/macos dirs exist but no T7/T8 binfmt path).
closure_criteria: On x86_64 host, an ARM64 T7/T8 container starts and `uname -m`=aarch64 and the agent responds to health check; before=no container, after=running ARM64 agent; capture container start + arch output with run UUID.

title: Build device profile registry with versioned YAML schema for T1-T8
description: Centralized YAML registry (device-registry.yaml) defining per-tier: name, trust_model (FULL/SEMI/STANDARD/EDGE_DONOR), simulator, architecture, resources (vcpus/memory_mb/disk_gb), network (bandwidth/latency), snapshot golden_image, and constraints (gpu/tee/npu/big_little/protocol_only/physical_required_for). Consumed by DevicePool at startup. Existing pkg/testing/device profile.go is PARTIAL (data-only registry with load/save/merge, T1-T8).
closure_criteria: Loading the registry yields 8 validated tier profiles each with correct simulator+resources; before=no profiles, after=8 parsed profiles; capture a registry dump for all 8 tiers + a rejected malformed-profile error with run UUID.

title: Implement automated tier detection validating host KVM/ARM64/binfmt capabilities
description: Before any provisioning, DevicePool validates the host can satisfy a requested tier (KVM accel present, ARM64 support for T6, binfmt registered for T7/T8) and returns an actionable error rather than failing mid-provision. Target >=99% detection accuracy with zero false positives for unsupported configs.
closure_criteria: Requesting T6 on a host without ARM64/KVM is rejected pre-provision with a typed error, while a supported request proceeds; before=silent failure, after=guarded rejection; capture both the rejection error and the successful path with run UUID.

title: Implement device provisioning lifecycle abstraction (Provisioner/Instance state machine)
description: Per GAP_AUDIT gap #5: add a Provisioner interface (Provision(*Profile)(Instance,error)) and Instance.Boot/Stop/Status with a deterministic FakeProvisioner state machine (provisioned->booting->ready->stopped) honoring profile boot times against a virtual clock. Lets controller/CLI exercise lifecycle without Firecracker/QEMU. Registry is currently data-only with no Provision/Boot/Spawn.
closure_criteria: Provision a T3 profile and observe state transitions provisioned->booting->ready; Boot from 'stopped' is rejected; profile boot-time honored on virtual clock; capture the transition trace and the rejected illegal transition with run UUID.

title: Implement unified golden snapshot + COW instant-reset across all simulator backends
description: SnapshotManager dispatches create_golden/instant_reset by tier to FirecrackerManager (snapshot/restore API), QemuManager (qcow2 external COW overlay discard+recreate), and DockerManager (image commit/reset). Targets: <=50ms reset for Firecracker, <=500ms QEMU qcow2 overlay (<=10ms file-recreate per sec01), <=2s Docker. Existing pkg/testing/snapshot is DONE for golden-file snapshotting only (not VM-state).
closure_criteria: For each backend, reset a dirtied instance to its golden state and confirm the dirty change is gone; before=mutated state, after=pristine; capture per-tier reset latency and a content diff proving reset with run UUID.

title: Implement qcow2 copy-on-write overlay management with 10-deep chain limit
description: Provide gold-image qcow2 base (read-only) plus per-session COW overlays created via qemu-img create -b base, with instant_reset that deletes the overlay and recreates the header (~10ms). Inspect chain via qemu-img info --backing-chain; cap chain depth at 10 overlays to avoid lookup degradation.
closure_criteria: Create base+overlay, write data to overlay, reset (discard+recreate), confirm written data is gone in ~10ms; before=overlay has deltas, after=clean overlay; capture backing-chain output + reset timing with run UUID.

title: Build Rust DST engine: single-threaded SimLoop with virtual clock and seeded PRNG
description: Implement the deterministic event loop (SimLoop): BinaryHeap event queue, SimInstant virtual clock advanced only when all actors block, SeededRng, SimulatedNetwork/SimulatedDisk, node handles, and invariant list. spawn_node + run(max_duration) returning SimResult (Success or InvariantViolated{invariant,at_time,seed}). The Go pkg/testing/dst engine is a PARTIAL in-repo substitute (real min-heap, seeded rand, virtual clock, deterministic replay) but is not the Rust turmoil core and is wired only to the CLI.
closure_criteria: Run a 100-node simulation twice with the same seed and obtain bit-identical event traces / SimResult; before=nondeterministic, after=100% reproducible; capture two identical run hashes for one seed and divergence for a different seed, tagged with run UUID.

title: Integrate Rust turmoil for deterministic simulated TCP/UDP networking
description: Wire turmoil (Tokio team) as the simulated network backend providing deterministic async TCP/UDP with configurable fail_rate, min/max message latency, host/client spawning, partition/heal/bounce. Drives consensus and scheduler simulation. Shuttle (thread-interleaving) and madsim are listed as complementary toolkit members.
closure_criteria: A turmoil-hosted 5-node consensus sim runs split-brain-recovery with seed S deterministically and partition injection alters node liveness identically across two seed-S runs; capture identical invariant outcomes for two runs + the seed with run UUID.

title: Implement INetwork/HelixNetwork trait with production and simulation swappable impls
description: Define HelixNetwork trait (bind/connect/send_to/recv_from + inject_partition/heal_partition/set_latency) with ProdNetwork (Tokio real stack, feature off) and SimNetwork (turmoil deterministic, feature='simulation') selected at compile time, so identical HelixCluster source runs in prod and sim (FoundationDB Net2/Sim2 pattern). GAP_AUDIT: interface swapping (Net2/Sim2) is MISSING — no Sim2/Net2/SimNet in any .go; distributed pkgs lack a sim transport seam.
closure_criteria: The same node code compiles+runs under both feature flags; in sim, inject_partition is consulted and partitions a node deterministically; before=no seam, after=prod/sim parity; capture both build outputs + a sim partition effect with run UUID.

title: Wire DST sim transport seam into pkg/swim membership (prod+sim parity)
description: Per GAP_AUDIT gap #2: define a Transport interface (Send(from,to,msg)) with a production net impl and a SimTransport backed by Engine.SendMessage/handlers, then run pkg/swim membership over it to realize 'same code in prod and sim' without external infra, consulting a chaos.NetworkPartition predicate.
closure_criteria: Run SWIM over SimTransport with seed S, partition two nodes, and assert the partitioned node is marked suspect/dead deterministically and identically across two seed-S runs; capture the two identical membership traces + seed with run UUID.

title: Implement BUGGIFY macro framework with ~25% deterministic fire rate
description: Provide buggify!{body} macro that fires ~25% of the time (random%4==0) driven by the engine seeded PRNG when is_buggify_enabled(), scattered at timeout/retry/error paths to force rare code (e.g. 60s->0.1s, 600x compression), corrupted-log and duplicate-append responses. GAP_AUDIT: BUGGIFY MISSING (no BUGGIFY in repo). Go variant per gap #3: Engine.Buggify(p float64) bool driven by eng.rng with a registration list.
closure_criteria: With a fixed seed, Buggify(0.5) yields a known exact boolean sequence over N calls and is always false when disabled; before=cold timeout paths, after=routinely exercised; capture the deterministic boolean sequence + a fresh-seed difference with run UUID.

title: Implement 10:1 DST virtual-time compression by fast-forwarding idle periods
description: Advance simulated time only when all actors are blocked on I/O, achieving 10:1 simulated:wall-clock ratio (1h->6min, 24h->2.4h). Risk mitigation: support batch processing of independent events and sharding across multiple DST processes if compression falls below 8:1 at 1,000 nodes.
closure_criteria: Run a 1-hour simulated workload and measure wall-clock <=6 min (>=10:1); validate at 100/500/1000 nodes; before=unmeasured, after=ratio >=10:1; capture the measured compression ratio per node count with run UUID.

title: Achieve 1,000+ simulated nodes in a single DST process
description: Scale the DST engine to run 1,000+ simulated cluster nodes in one process without VM overhead (~2MB/node, 100,000+ events/sec, <1ms invariant check per step), enabling large-cluster consensus/scheduler validation cheaply.
closure_criteria: Spawn 1,000 simulated nodes in a single process and run a workload to completion within memory budget; before=VM-bound scale, after=1000 in-process nodes; capture node count, RSS, and events/sec with run UUID.

title: Author DST consensus+gossip workloads using SETUP→EXECUTION→CHECK→METRICS pattern
description: Implement the FoundationDB 4-phase workload pattern (TOML/Rust-defined): SETUP spawn_nodes+wait_for_quorum, EXECUTION with random partition/node-crash chaos + task storm, CHECK invariants (NoLostTasks all_tasks_scheduled, NoDoubleAssignment, quorum>=3), METRICS (throughput tasks/sec, latency p99). Target >=90% protocol code-path coverage.
closure_criteria: Run consensus_survives_random_partitions(seed) to green with invariants asserted (unscheduled==0, no double-assign, healthy>=quorum); before=untested protocol, after=invariants enforced; capture passing run + the reproducible seed with run UUID.

title: Build Elixir/OTP Chaos Controller GenServer with supervision-tree isolation
description: Implement HelixChaos.Controller GenServer with state machine [idle,setup,running,paused,recovering,completed,failed], API load_scenario/start_experiment/emergency_stop/get_status, blast_radius target selection (take_random of healthy targets * blast_radius), schedule_faults via Process.send_after, and auto_recover timer. GAP_AUDIT: Elixir controller MISSING/DEFERRED (no .ex/mix.exs).
closure_criteria: Load a scenario and start an experiment that injects faults against a bounded target set then auto-recovers; before=no faults, after=faults injected+healed; capture controller state transitions and target/blast-radius log with run UUID.

title: Implement 8 network fault injectors (latency, loss, corruption, reorder, dup, bandwidth, partition, DNS, TCP reset)
description: Implement network fault types via tc netem / tc tbf / iptables-nftables / Chaos Mesh DNSChaos / tcpkill: NF-01 latency (delay/jitter/dist), NF-02 packet loss (percent/correlation), NF-03 corruption, NF-04 reordering (percent/gap), packet duplication, NF-05/06 bandwidth limit, network partition (direction/duration), NF-07 DNS failure, NF-08 TCP reset. GAP_AUDIT: chaos PARTIAL — only 5 in-process boolean faults exist, no real netem/iptables effects.
closure_criteria: Each network fault is injected against a live target and produces the measurable effect (e.g. tc shows added delay; partition drops connectivity) then is healed; before=normal traffic, after=degraded then restored; capture tc/iptables state + ping/latency deltas per fault with run UUID.

title: Implement 8 node fault injectors (VM crash/restart/pause, CPU/mem/disk pressure, OOM kill, graceful shutdown)
description: Implement node faults via QMP and stress-ng/fio/cgroups: NF-09 VM crash (system_powerdown), NF-10 restart (system_reset repeat), NF-11 pause (stop/cont), NF-12 CPU pressure (stress-ng), NF-13 memory pressure (stress-ng --vm), NF-14 disk pressure (fio+loopback fill), NF-15 OOM kill (cgroups memory.limit), NF-16 graceful shutdown. Each must be recoverable without manual intervention.
closure_criteria: Each node fault is injected against a real VM/container and the cluster detects+recovers (e.g. crashed node re-elected/rescheduled); before=healthy, after=faulted then recovered; capture QMP/stress-ng invocation + cluster recovery evidence with run UUID.

title: Implement 3 time fault injectors (clock skew, clock freeze, monotonic drift)
description: Implement time faults: NF-17 clock skew via Chaos Mesh TimeChaos (offset_sec, clock_ids REALTIME/MONOTONIC, VDSO interception per-container), NF-18 clock freeze (duration), NF-19 monotonic drift via libfaketime (speed_factor). Tests lease/TTL/causal-ordering robustness. GAP_AUDIT lists clock-skew among the missing 20 fault types.
closure_criteria: Inject -600s clock skew on a subset of pods without affecting host clock; the lease/heartbeat manager detects inconsistency and avoids split-brain; before=synced clocks, after=skewed-then-reset; capture clock offset evidence + lease-manager response with run UUID.

title: Implement 6 hardware fault injectors (NMI, mem CE/UE, PCIe AER, CPU bit-flip, thermal throttle)
description: Implement hardware faults: NF-20 NMI injection (QMP inject-nmi), NF-21 memory correctable error (EDAC sysfs), NF-22 memory uncorrectable error (mce-inject), NF-23 PCIe AER (QMP pcie_aer_inject_error), NF-24 CPU bit-flip (custom QEMU module, register/bit), NF-25 thermal throttle (cpufreq governor max_freq). Tests panic handling, error counting, I/O retry, fault tolerance, perf degradation.
closure_criteria: Inject each hardware fault on a QEMU VM and observe the targeted system response (e.g. EDAC error count increments; cpufreq cap reduces clock); before=nominal hardware state, after=fault recorded; capture sysfs/QMP evidence per fault with run UUID.

title: Implement pure-Go in-sim chaos faults toward 25+ (ClockSkew, DiskFill, MessageReorder, Byzantine, etc.)
description: Per GAP_AUDIT gap #1: extend pkg/testing/chaos with pure-Go in-sim faults on the existing Fault interface: ClockSkew, DiskFill, MessageReorder, MessageDuplication, ByzantineCorruption, DNSFailure, CertExpiry, SlowDisk, Bitflip, ConnectionReset. Each holds parameters + applied state and exposes a query (ShouldCorrupt(), Skew()) the DST engine consults, preserving apply/restore symmetry and ChaosRunner. Only 5 fault structs exist today (20 short of target).
closure_criteria: With a fixed RNG, ClockSkew.Skew() returns the exact deterministic offset sequence and is zero before Apply()/after Restore(); before=5 faults, after=>=15 faults; capture the deterministic offset sequence + before/after guard behavior with run UUID.
source_refs: phase_04/GAP_AUDIT.md (TOP IMPLEMENTABLE GAPS #1; 25+ fault types row)

title: Build YAML chaos Scenario Engine with phases, blast radius and abort-on-SLO-breach
description: Implement ScenarioEngine parsing ChaosScenario YAML (apiVersion helixcluster.io/v1): blast_radius (0.0-1.0), duration_sec, abort_on_slo_breach, target_selector (match_tiers, min_trust_level, exclude_labels), ordered phases (baseline/inject_faults/heal_all with per-fault params+target_percent), and success_criteria assertions with severity. Translates to scheduled fault-injection events with auto-recovery sequencing.
closure_criteria: A 5-phase scenario (baseline->latency->partial-partition->severe-partition->recovery) executes end-to-end honoring blast_radius and aborts if an SLO assertion breaks; before=no scenario, after=phased execution; capture per-phase fault log + success_criteria evaluation with run UUID.

title: Implement emergency-stop and auto-recovery with <=2s halt latency
description: emergency_stop cast halts all NetworkFault/NodeFault/TimeFault/HardwareFault injectors and runs recover_all + heal_all, transitioning to :recovering. auto_recover timer (Process.send_after duration_sec*1000) restores faults on schedule. Must halt all active faults within <=2 seconds.
closure_criteria: With multiple faults active, issuing emergency_stop halts and heals all within <=2s; before=active faults, after=all healed; capture timestamped fault-active->healed transition (<=2s) with run UUID.

title: Integrate Chaos Mesh CRDs (NetworkChaos, TimeChaos, StressChaos, DNSChaos)
description: Deploy Chaos Mesh v2.6+ into K3s and drive NetworkChaos (partition mode/selector/direction/target), TimeChaos (timeOffset/clockIds, random-max-percent), StressChaos (cpu workers/load), DNSChaos via CRDs, integrated through the Elixir controller and RBAC for chaos-mesh.org/*. Provides TimeChaos VDSO clock-skew unavailable to in-process faults.
closure_criteria: Apply a NetworkChaos partition + TimeChaos skew CR against helix-agent pods and observe the cluster react (split-brain prevented) then CR deletion heals; before=no CR, after=chaos applied+removed; capture kubectl chaos CR status + cluster behavior with run UUID.

title: Build Virtual Testing Controller OTP supervision tree (one_for_all)
description: Implement HelixTest.Application supervisor (strategy one_for_all) wiring SessionManager, DevicePool, TestRunner, StateMachine, SnapshotManager, MetricsCollector, HelixChaos.Controller + fault servers + ScenarioEngine, Web.Endpoint, Phoenix.PubSub, and Cluster.Supervisor (libcluster). GAP_AUDIT: internal/testing/{controller,dashboard,faults,workloads} MISSING.
closure_criteria: Boot the OTP app; all child GenServers start and a forced child crash triggers one_for_all restart restoring consistency; before=no controller, after=running supervised tree; capture supervisor child list + restart event with run UUID.

title: Implement SessionManager with 50-session cap, 2h TTL, resource-quota enforcement
description: SessionManager GenServer: create_session/destroy_session/get_session, @max_sessions 50, @default_ttl 2h, shared resource_pool (firecracker_vms 500, qemu_vms 48, docker_containers 200, total_memory_mb 256000, total_vcpus 192), TTL sweeper every 5min, device reclamation + resource merge on destroy. Prevents oversubscription.
closure_criteria: Creating sessions beyond the cap returns :max_sessions_reached; destroying a session reclaims its devices+resources; an expired session is swept; before=unbounded, after=quota-enforced; capture cap rejection + reclamation log + sweep event with run UUID.

title: Implement DevicePool GenServer with tier-to-simulator dispatch and health checks
description: DevicePool: provision_devices(session_id,tier_spec)/destroy_device, initialize per-simulator pools (firecracker t1/t2/t3, qemu t4/t5/t6, docker t7/t8), dispatch provision_tier by simulator (firecracker/qemu_kvm/docker_protocol/cuttlefish), health_summary, release/reclaim, and health monitoring.
closure_criteria: provision_devices for each tier returns live device handles via the correct backend and health_summary reflects them; before=empty pool, after=allocated devices; capture provisioning dispatch log + health summary with run UUID.

title: Implement TestRunner with parallel suite execution and result collection
description: TestRunner GenServer: run_suite(session,suite_def) runs setup phase (provision_devices/wait_for_quorum/load_snapshot) then Task.async_stream tests with max_concurrency (parallelism||4) and timeout, dispatching by test type (dst_workload, chaos_scenario, network_test, consistency_check), and collects passed/failed into a report (suite,session,total,passed,failed,timestamp).
closure_criteria: Run a mixed suite (dst+chaos) and obtain a report with correct passed/failed counts and per-test durations; before=no execution, after=report produced; capture the suite report JSON with run UUID.

title: Implement session test state machine (IDLE→SETUP→RUNNING→CHAOS_INJECT→VERIFY→RECOVERY→REPORT)
description: Implement the finite state machine governing valid session transitions and entry/exit actions: IDLE->SETUP (provision)->RUNNING->CHAOS_INJECT<->RUNNING->VERIFY (invariants)->RECOVERY/REPORT->IDLE, plus FAILED for unrecoverable errors. Defines legal transitions per the state table.
closure_criteria: A session traverses the full lifecycle with illegal transitions rejected; before=ad-hoc state, after=enforced FSM; capture the recorded transition sequence + a rejected illegal transition with run UUID.

title: Expose REST API for session CRUD, device provisioning and snapshot restore
description: Phoenix Web.Endpoint exposes REST API: session create/destroy/get, POST /api/v1/devices/provision (single call provisioning any of the 8 tiers), snapshot restore, plus CI-webhook and scheduled triggers feeding the controller. Port 4000 http / 4001 rpc.
closure_criteria: All eight tiers are provisionable through a single POST /api/v1/devices/provision call and session CRUD works over HTTP; before=no API, after=working endpoints; capture HTTP request/response for provision-all-tiers + session lifecycle with run UUID.

title: Build Phoenix LiveView real-time test dashboard
description: TestDashboardLive subscribes to PubSub topics (test:events, device:health, chaos:faults) and renders real-time active sessions, active tests, device health, chaos fault status, and metrics over WebSocket. Leverages BEAM's 2M+ concurrent WebSocket capacity; no external broker. GAP_AUDIT: Phoenix LiveView dashboard MISSING/DEFERRED.
closure_criteria: With a live test running, the dashboard updates session/device/chaos state in real time as events fire; before=no visibility, after=live updates visible; capture before/after dashboard screenshots reflecting an injected fault with run UUID.

title: Implement MetricsCollector exporting 15+ chaos Prometheus metric series with OpenTelemetry tracing
description: Prometheus-compatible MetricsCollector scraped at 15s via ServiceMonitor; chaos controller emits 15+ metric series (fault injection rates, target device health, recovery latency). OpenTelemetry distributed tracing spans the Rust/Elixir/Go polyglot boundary; Grafana dashboards for test progress/device health/chaos/DST perf.
closure_criteria: During a chaos experiment, Prometheus scrapes >=15 distinct helix_chaos_* series and a trace spans controller->DST->device; before=no metrics, after=series+trace present; capture /metrics scrape listing >=15 series + a trace view with run UUID.

title: Implement HelixQA automatic challenge generation from test outcomes
description: ChallengeGenerator.generate_from_report produces safety_invariant challenges (id chaos-{session}-{invariant}, embeds seed+scenario+at_time, reproducibility :deterministic, dst_replay harness) and performance_regression challenges, with severity->points mapping (critical 500/high 300/warning 150/info 50). GAP_AUDIT: HelixQA integration MISSING.
closure_criteria: A failed safety invariant during chaos auto-generates a HelixQA challenge within 60s embedding the reproducible seed; before=no challenge, after=challenge present in HelixQA; capture the generated challenge object + replay-from-seed proof with run UUID.

title: Implement metrics validation against baseline KPI table with severity gating
description: Validate run metrics against the baseline table: helix_nodes_healthy>=floor(total*0.5)+1 (critical), helix_tasks_unscheduled==0 (critical) and rate<1 (warning), schedule_latency p99<1000ms, consensus_rounds rate<10, test_duration p95<300s, firecracker_vcpu<80%, chaos_faults_injected>=1, recovery_time p99<30000ms. Violations at/above severity fail CI quality gate.
closure_criteria: Injecting a metric that breaches a critical rule produces a quality-gate failure while in-range metrics pass; before=ungated, after=gated; capture the validation report flagging the breach + a passing run with run UUID.

title: Implement Welch's t-test statistical regression detector for HelixQA
description: Per GAP_AUDIT gap #4: new pkg/testing/regression implementing Welch(a,b)->(t,dfWelch,p) and a Detector flagging regression when p<alpha (0.05) AND mean degrades beyond a threshold (>10% change), over rolling baselines of >=10 samples, returning a structured result the challenge pipeline publishes (dual-threshold to avoid false positives). Target false-positive rate <=5%. GAP_AUDIT: regression engine MISSING.
closure_criteria: Fed a textbook two-sample fixture, Welch() returns the published t-stat/p-value within epsilon and identical distributions yield 'no regression'; before=no detector, after=regression flagged correctly; capture computed t/p vs expected + a no-regression case with run UUID.
source_refs: phase_04/GAP_AUDIT.md (TOP IMPLEMENTABLE GAPS #4; HelixQA regression row)

title: Integrate CI/CD quality gates for GitHub Actions / GitLab CI / Jenkins
description: Native CI integration: GitHub Actions workflow (dst-smoke -> tier-matrix[T1..T8] -> regression-gate posting PR comment), GitLab CI (test_smoke->test_full parallel matrix->regression_gate allow_failure:false), webhook-driven session initiation. DST smoke gates the tier matrix which gates regression analysis; CI blocks merge on >10% regression. mix helix.test.* tasks (dst/check/provision/chaos/metrics/regression).
closure_criteria: A PR with an injected >10% regression is blocked by the CI gate and a results comment is posted; a clean PR passes; before=no gate, after=merge blocked on regression; capture the failing CI run + PR comment + a passing run with run UUID.

title: Build WebAssembly plugin host on Wasmtime Component Model with WIT bindings
description: Implement the Wasmtime host runtime loading wasm32-wasi component plugins via WIT (package helix:cluster@1.0.0) with a plugin registry, resource limits, and capability auth. Plugins authored in Rust/Go/Zig/C++ implement standard interfaces. Existing pkg/wasm is PARTIAL->strong (genuine wasmtime-go/v29 engine, WASI load/instantiate, plugin ABI into real linear memory) but lacks Component Model / WIT bindings.
closure_criteria: Load a real .wasm device-simulator component and invoke create/get-state/reset returning guest-computed values; before=no plugin, after=plugin executes; capture the host loading the component + a round-trip call result with run UUID.

title: Define WIT interfaces for device-simulator, workload-generator, fault-injector, metrics-exporter
description: Author helix-cluster-plugin.wit defining four interfaces with typed records: device-simulator (device-config, device-state, health-status variant, create/destroy/get-state/reset/apply-fault, fault-params), workload-generator (workload-config, task-spec, task-result, generate-tasks/validate-result), fault-injector (fault-config, active-fault, inject/heal/get-active-faults), metrics-exporter (metric, export-format enum, export/configure), and the helix-plugin world importing all four. Plugin type matrix maps categories to required interfaces.
closure_criteria: The WIT compiles and generates host+guest bindings; a plugin implementing device-simulator validates against the contract; before=no contract, after=compiled bindings; capture wit-bindgen output + a conforming plugin build with run UUID.

title: Implement capability-based plugin sandbox with resource limits and audit logging
description: Per GAP_AUDIT gap #7 + plugin-security-policy.yaml: enforce capability grants (network default off w/ max_bandwidth+allowed_ports, filesystem read-only allowed_paths, clock off=simulated time, random on=deterministic PRNG), resource_limits (memory 128MB, cpu 10%, execution_timeout 5000ms, max_concurrent_calls 4), isolation (memory/namespace/seccomp), audit (log_all_calls, log_fault_injections, 30d retention). Wasmtime enforces at WASI syscall boundary. Add a spawn benchmark (target 5us).
closure_criteria: A plugin importing a denied host function fails to instantiate with a typed error while an allowed plugin succeeds; before=full WASI always, after=gated; capture the denied-instantiate error + allowed success + 5us spawn benchmark with run UUID.

title: Provide reference plugins (Rust device-sim, Zig device-sim) compiled to wasm32-wasi
description: Provide buildable example plugins demonstrating the SDK: Rust CustomDeviceSimulator (create/destroy/get_state/reset/apply_fault, export! macro) and Zig DeviceSimulator (StringHashMap of device state, create/destroy/reset), each compiled to wasm32-wasi, proving language-agnostic authoring.
closure_criteria: Both example plugins build to .wasm and load+run in the host returning expected device-state; before=no examples, after=two working plugins; capture build artifacts + host invocation outputs with run UUID.

title: Implement cmd/helix-test CLI with dst/chaos/device/snapshot subcommands
description: helix-test CLI (DONE per GAP_AUDIT: cmd/helix-test/main.go run(args,stdout,stderr)int seam, honest seed/arg validation, tested). Subcommands dst/chaos/device/snapshot exercise the testing primitives end-to-end. Maintain and extend coverage as new primitives land.
closure_criteria: Running `helix-test dst run --seed S` and `helix-test chaos run` produces deterministic, validated output and correct exit codes; before=no CLI, after=usable CLI; capture command invocations + exit codes for each subcommand with run UUID.

title: Build cmd/helix-snapshot standalone CLI reusing pkg/testing/snapshot
description: Per GAP_AUDIT gap #6: promote the snapshot subcommand into its own P1 binary cmd/helix-snapshot reusing pkg/testing/snapshot, with the same injectable run(args,stdout,stderr)int seam as helix-test. Standalone binary currently MISSING (folded informally into helix-test snapshot).
closure_criteria: A create->list->compare(match)->compare(mismatch->exit1)->delete sequence over a temp dir via the run seam asserts correct exit codes and stdout; before=no binary, after=standalone CLI; capture the command sequence + exit codes (incl. exit 1 on mismatch) with run UUID.

title: Build cmd/helix-testd daemon as OTP controller node entrypoint
description: Implement cmd/helix-testd daemon (OTP controller node) that hosts the Virtual Testing Controller services as a long-running process exposing the REST/RPC endpoints and joining the libcluster mesh. GAP_AUDIT: helix-testd MISSING (absent from cmd).
closure_criteria: Starting helix-testd brings up the controller, accepts a session-create request, and stays healthy; before=no daemon, after=running daemon serving requests; capture daemon startup log + a served API call with run UUID.

title: Implement Firecracker MicroVM Kubernetes operator and CRD
description: Define microvms.firecracker.helixcluster.io CRD (spec: tier enum T1-T3, vcpus 1-8, memoryMb 128-16384, kernelImage, rootfsImage, network bridge/macAddress, snapshot enabled/goldenSnapshot; status: phase Pending..Failed, vmId, ipAddress) and a controller reconciling MicroVM resources into running Firecracker VMs.
closure_criteria: Applying a MicroVM CR provisions a Firecracker VM and the operator updates status.phase to Running with an ipAddress; before=CR only, after=running VM; capture kubectl get microvm status transitions with run UUID.

title: Deploy WireGuard encrypted inter-host mesh DaemonSet for multi-host clusters
description: DaemonSet (hostNetwork, NET_ADMIN/SYS_MODULE) configuring WireGuard interfaces per test host with Kubernetes-based peer discovery, subnet 10.200.0.0/16, port 51820, cluster key from secret. Spans test clusters across physical hosts as one flat network (WAN latency configurable via tc netem) and encrypts all inter-host test traffic.
closure_criteria: Two test hosts join the mesh and pods on different hosts communicate over the encrypted 10.200/16 subnet; before=isolated hosts, after=meshed connectivity; capture wg show peer handshake + cross-host ping with run UUID.

title: Implement distributed snapshot pool backend (MinIO) and multi-host scheduling
description: Multi-host config: etcd cluster for distributed state, MinIO-backed distributed snapshot pool (helix-snapshots bucket), spread scheduler policy with max_sessions_per_host=10 and per-host capacity (memory 512000MB, 96 vCPUs, 500 firecracker, 12 qemu). libcluster Kubernetes discovery + HPA (3-10 replicas, CPU 70%/mem 80%).
closure_criteria: A golden snapshot stored on one host is restored on another via MinIO and sessions spread across hosts per policy; before=local-only snapshots, after=shared pool restore; capture cross-host snapshot restore + scheduler spread placement with run UUID.

title: Implement vsock host-guest control channel for chaos-resilient telemetry
description: Implement vsock-based host<->guest communication that bypasses the network stack so the orchestrator can send commands/receive telemetry from simulated nodes even when their network interfaces are partitioned/latency/loss-injected (control plane stays reachable during network chaos).
closure_criteria: With a node's virtio-net under full partition, the controller still issues commands and reads telemetry over vsock; before=control lost under partition, after=control retained; capture a vsock round-trip during an active network partition with run UUID.

title: Implement Mininet WAN topology harness for multi-region network-stack testing
description: Provide a Mininet Python topology (HelixClusterWANTopo: n_regions x nodes_per_region, region switches, WAN links with per-link delay/bw/loss e.g. 70/150/220ms) running real HelixCluster binaries in network namespaces over the actual Linux kernel stack, committable to CI for network-topology/partition validation.
closure_criteria: Stand up a 3-region/15-node Mininet topology and run agents that experience the configured WAN latencies; before=no topology test, after=multi-region behavior observed; capture ping latencies matching link config + agent cross-region behavior with run UUID.

title: Author TLA+/PlusCal formal specs for leader election and scheduler allocation
description: Model HelixCluster's consensus/leader-election (HelixLeaderElection module: AtMostOneLeader, LeaderConnected safety invariants over StartElection/WinElection/Partition/Heal) and the scheduler allocation logic in TLA+/PlusCal, checked exhaustively by TLC before implementation to catch design-level bugs (per AWS 35-step DynamoDB precedent).
closure_criteria: TLC exhaustively checks the spec for a bounded node set and reports the invariants hold (or yields a counterexample trace that is then fixed); before=unverified design, after=model-checked; capture the TLC run summary (states explored, invariants OK) with run UUID.

title: Author Jepsen black-box linearizability test for task scheduling under partitions
description: Build a Jepsen test (HelixClient with schedule/cancel/status ops, partition-random-halves nemesis, phased generator warm-up/chaos/recovery, checker/linearizable) that verifies the deployed HelixCluster's scheduling operations remain linearizable under random network partitions.
closure_criteria: Run the Jepsen test against a 5-node deployment under partition and the linearizable checker reports a valid history (or a real anomaly to fix); before=no black-box check, after=linearizability verified; capture the Jepsen analysis verdict with run UUID.

title: Integrate Shadow/Phantom for unmodified-binary deterministic network simulation
description: Use Shadow (Phantom v2) to run the actual unmodified HelixCluster node binary as native processes inside a deterministic discrete-event simulation (seccomp+LD_PRELOAD syscall interception, ~40MB/node, 1,000-node sims) with configurable topology/latency/faults, bridging DST and chaos without code changes.
closure_criteria: Run the real node binary in a 100+ node Shadow simulation that reproduces identically across re-runs of one config; before=no binary-level sim, after=deterministic binary sim; capture two identical Shadow run outputs + node count with run UUID.

title: Add property-based + coverage-guided fuzzing for cluster operations
description: Combine proptest-style state-machine property testing (random sequences of submit_task/node_join/node_fail/network_partition verifying idempotency, monotonicity, consistency, no double-assignment, no task loss) with Syzkaller-style coverage-guided fuzzing treating cluster operations as fuzzable 'syscalls' to explore failure-handling paths the scheduler's complex branching (affinity/anti-affinity/priority preemption/GPU alloc) hides.
closure_criteria: The fuzzer/proptest generates thousands of randomized op sequences and finds no safety-invariant violation (or surfaces one to fix); before=human-written cases only, after=stochastic coverage; capture coverage growth + invariant-check summary with run UUID.

title: Add eBPF/XDP line-rate programmable network fault injection (cilium/ebpf)
description: Use cilium/ebpf (pure-Go, no CGO) with bpf2go to load/attach XDP programs at the NIC driver level for line-rate fault injection (drop 0.1% of heartbeat packets between node pairs, reorder TCP segments, inject latency) and eBPF tracepoints for zero-instrumentation per-process CPU/mem/network observability of the system under test.
closure_criteria: Attach an XDP program that drops a configured fraction of packets between two nodes and observe the measured drop rate + retry behavior; before=no kernel-level fault, after=line-rate drops applied; capture eBPF map config + measured packet drop stats with run UUID.

title: Validate gem5 big.LITTLE (O3+Minor) scheduler fidelity for RK3588
description: Use gem5's SimpleSwitchableProcessor (O3 representing Cortex-A76 cluster, Minor/TIMING representing Cortex-A55) to validate HelixCluster scheduler decisions on a genuine heterogeneous big.LITTLE topology that QEMU cannot model (QEMU requires homogeneous vCPUs; MIDR not overridable). Accepts slow simulation in exchange for architectural fidelity.
closure_criteria: Boot a gem5 ARM full-system model with mixed O3+Minor cores and run the scheduler, observing core-type-aware placement decisions; before=homogeneous-only testing, after=heterogeneous validation; capture gem5 core-type assignment + scheduler decision trace with run UUID.

title: Evaluate VirGL/Venus virtual GPU for OpenGL/Vulkan workload functional testing
description: Use virglrenderer (OpenGL 4.3/GLES 3.2) and Venus (Vulkan via Zink) with QEMU virtio-gpu-gl to functionally test GPU-dependent workloads on RK3588-proxied VMs (shader compilation, basic GPU compute, ROCm/HSA virtualization) at ~50-80% native perf; document that performance characterization of Mali-G610 still requires physical hardware.
closure_criteria: Run an OpenGL ES / Vulkan workload inside a VirGL/Venus-enabled VM and confirm it renders/computes correctly; before=no virtual GPU path, after=functional GPU workload; capture rendered output / compute result + perf ratio note with run UUID.

title: Integrate Tart OCI-native macOS/Linux VMs for iOS/macOS CI build-and-test
description: Use Tart (Apple Virtualization.framework, OCI registry pull/push of VM images, ~2-3x faster than GitHub-hosted macOS runners) for iOS agent build-and-test cycles and ARM64 Linux validation on Apple Silicon, with Vetu extending Tart Linux VMs to x86_64/ARM64 Linux hosts via Cloud Hypervisor.
closure_criteria: Clone a Tart macOS/Linux VM from an OCI registry, run an iOS agent build, and SSH to verify; before=no Apple CI VM, after=ephemeral OCI VM building agent; capture tart run + build success output with run UUID.

title: Define Corellium / physical-hardware-in-the-loop path for iOS, PS4, RK3588 GPU/NPU
description: Document and wire the hardware-in-the-loop strategy for fidelity-bound tiers with no software emulation: iOS true virtualization via Corellium ($9,995+ enterprise) or physical iOS for sensor/background/push; physical PS4/PS5 devkits as special-tier nodes; physical Orange Pi 5 Max for Mali-G610 GPU/6 TOPS NPU/VPU. Hybrid controller manages ~90% simulated + ~10% physical nodes under one abstraction with uniform health monitoring + chaos.
closure_criteria: The controller registers a physical (or Corellium) device as a special-tier node that passes health checks and receives chaos injection like simulated nodes; before=sim-only fleet, after=hybrid fleet; capture the physical node registration + health/chaos evidence with run UUID.

title: Benchmark Firecracker 5,000+ microVMs per host with KSM and memory overcommit
description: Demonstrate the success-criteria density target: 5,000+ Firecracker microVMs simultaneously managed on a single host (KSM tuning, 20x memory oversubscription, snapshot pool caching). 2,000 micro smoke VMs (1vCPU/128MB) on a 256GB host as an intermediate point. GAP_AUDIT: success-criteria benchmarks MISSING.
closure_criteria: On a 96-core/512GB host, launch and manage 5,000+ microVMs concurrently and confirm responsiveness; before=unmeasured, after=>=5000 VMs live; capture VM count, host RAM with KSM dedup savings, and per-VM responsiveness with run UUID.

title: Run 72-hour continuous chaos soak proving no resource leaks or degradation
description: Production-hardening success criterion: sustain a 72-hour continuous chaos experiment across the full stack without resource leaks, memory growth, or performance degradation, with KSM tuning, parallel session execution, and snapshot pool caching applied.
closure_criteria: Run a 72h continuous chaos experiment and confirm stable memory/CPU/latency throughout with no leaks; before=untested longevity, after=72h stable; capture start/end resource graphs + leak check with run UUID.

title: Execute Production Readiness Review with 80-item checklist (>=95% complete)
description: Conduct the PRR covering 80 checklist items across reliability, observability, security, scalability, and maintainability, requiring >=95% completion with all critical items resolved; plus operator documentation (architecture runbooks, troubleshooting guides, API reference, dashboard manual) and operator training/drills enabling provision/execute/recover of a full 8-tier session without engineering assistance.
closure_criteria: PRR checklist reaches >=95% with zero open criticals and a trained operator independently runs a full 8-tier provision/execute/recover drill; before=no PRR, after=signed-off PRR; capture the completed checklist + operator drill result with run UUID.

title: Run full 8-tier matrix (160 nodes) end-to-end within 45-minute CI budget
description: Demonstrate the integration milestone: a full tier matrix across T1-T8 (160 nodes: 48 Firecracker + 12 QEMU + 100 Docker) — provision, chaos scenarios, metrics export, regression analysis — completes in <=45 minutes in CI per the workload-profile sizing table.
closure_criteria: A single CI run provisions all 8 tiers (160 nodes), runs chaos+metrics+regression, and finishes within 45 min; before=no full-matrix run, after=green matrix <=45min; capture the CI run duration + per-tier pass/fail summary with run UUID.

title: Define polyglot interop boundaries (Rust↔Go↔Elixir↔Wasm)
description: Establish the component-to-language interop contract: gRPC+FlatBuffers between Rust DST/consensus core and the Elixir/Go control plane (~100ns CGO overhead acceptable for coarse calls, gRPC for cleaner separation), WIT-generated bindings for host->plugin calls, and eBPF maps for kernel->userspace. Each boundary explicit, versioned, testable.
closure_criteria: A Rust consensus proposal crosses the gRPC/FlatBuffers boundary to the Go/Elixir control plane and back with correct serialization; before=undefined boundaries, after=working interop; capture a cross-language round-trip with payload integrity check and run UUID.

title: Integrate libcluster automatic BEAM cluster formation via Kubernetes DNS
description: Use libcluster (Kubernetes DNS strategy, 5s polling of helix-cluster-headless / helix-test-controller selector) so controller BEAM nodes auto-discover and connect as pods scale up/down, delivering :nodeup/:nodedown as standard messages and enabling distributed test execution + Phoenix distributed PubSub without an external broker.
closure_criteria: Scaling controller replicas causes new BEAM nodes to auto-join the cluster and a terminated pod is removed; before=manual clustering, after=auto-formed; capture Node.list() reflecting scale changes with run UUID.
